english: For many years there was a fight between the two houses. Then those two came together. This one said to that one: "Your brother killed my offspring, and my brother killed your offspring. Take the price, and I too shall take the price. Let there be peace for us." Then they drank wine together.
uncertain: h₁ést: PST.3SG 'was' (could also be AOR 'threw'; 'be' fits)
toy moy / moy toy: enclitic possessors; which goes with bʰréh₂tēr and which with ǵénh₁mn̥ is by position only ('your brother... my offspring', then reversed)
moréyet, gʷʰént: PST (ongoing) used for completed killings; read as simple past
polh₁úh₂ yóh₁r̥h₂: ACC.PL of duration 'for many years'
misfit: ph₃ént: AOR.3PL 'they drank', but the actors are the dual tóh₁ 'those two' (cf. dual gʷm̥tā́m); 3DU ph₃tā́m expected unless the whole households are meant (candidate, not certain)

english: A man sat at the fire and made an oath: "The sun has seen me, the fire heard me, the water knows me. I did not steal the wagon. If I speak a lie, may the fire burn me, may the water swallow me, and may the sun not see me."
uncertain: stéh₂yom: PST.1SG 'was stealing'; with ne read 'did not steal'

english: He who steals, the night hides him, but the sun has seen him. He who drives off horses, the dog knows him. The wolf comes at night; the shepherd is awake. A man who steals eats and is not satisfied.
uncertain: stéh₂yonts h₂nḗr: participle 'a stealing man' = a thief
misfit: gʷm̥yóh₂: PRS.1SG 'I come', but the subject is wĺ̥kʷos 'wolf' (3SG); 3SG gʷm̥yéti expected

english: Two brothers stood before the king. This one said: "These cattle are mine." That one said: "They are not yours, they are mine." Then he [the king] said: "Cattle know their own master. You two, call them." Then this one called, and they did not go. That one called, and they heard his voice and went to him. Then he said to that one: "They are yours."
uncertain: h₁stā́m: PST.3DU 'were (before)' or AOR of 'throw'; 'stood/were before' fits
HrudHtóm: PST.2DU or IMP.2DU; imperative fits
sékʷt: 'said' (homonym 'followed'); subject unnamed, taken as the king
h₁ím-kʷe gʷh₂ént: h₁ím ACC 'to him' as goal of motion

english: A brother is a brother's arm. He who kills his brother cuts off his own arm. A man has two arms; a house has two brothers. A lone sheep is the wolf's meat.
uncertain: h₂n̥réy ... h₁stés / démey h₁stés: dative of possession with dual 'be' ('to a man are two arms')
h₂r̥Hmós: NOM.SG 'arm' (analyzer also offers a verb PRS.1PL)

english: A woman went to the king and said: "My horse is gone." Then he said to the shepherd: "Track it." Then the shepherd tracked it along the path and found it in a man's enclosure. Then he [the king] said: "Your horse, how is it in the enclosure?" [The man:] "I found it on the path." "Did you tell the woman?" "I did not tell her." "Give it back to the woman. He who finds and does not speak, he steals."
uncertain: gʷḗn: only LEMMA analysis; taken as NOM.SG 'woman'
stéygʰm̥: ACC.SG 'path' (with énu 'along') vs AOR.1SG 'I climbed'; noun fits
toy: 'your horse' or 'to you'; position ambiguous
speakers unmarked in dialogue; assigned by sense

english: My master, hear my pledge. I shall guard your sheep for a year. I shall lead them to water and drive them home at night, and I shall stay awake at night and work for you. If a wolf seizes a sheep, I shall give you a sheep. If I deceive you, may the gods strike me down. Give me my wage.

Two women came to the king and spoke: "The sheep is mine." Then he said: "Shepherd, split the sheep in two." Then this one said: "Split it." That one cried out: "Do not split it! Let it be this one's, and let it live." Then he said: "I am her mistress. Take her."
uncertain: h₁ésmi: PRS.1SG 'I am'; also LOC.SG 'in him', which does not fit either
misfit: h₁ésmi: 1SG 'I am her mistress' in the judge's verdict (followed by 2SG IMP h₁áyso 'take her'); 2SG h₁ési 'you are' expected, and a feminine 'mistress' cannot be the male judge

english: Two fathers sat together and drank wine. This one gave that one a plough; that one gave this one a boat. Then this one said: "Let there be a bond between the two houses. May our sons be friends. Let no one break the pledge."
uncertain: Hrunépt: PST.3SG; with mē read as prohibitive injunctive

english: "Will you swear the oath?" "I shall swear it." "Whom do you fear?" "I fear Father Sky. He has seen what is hidden. If I deceive him, may he strike me down, and may my offspring not grow."
uncertain: dʰéh₁esi / dʰéh₁oh₂: SBJV 'will you place / I shall place (an oath)'
kudʰtóm: ACC.SG 'the hidden (thing)'; analyzer also offers IMP.2DU

english: The father-in-law and the son-in-law stood before the king. The father-in-law said: "He did not bring me the bride-price." "Son-in-law, did you give the bride-price?" "I gave ten cattle." "Who saw it?" "I saw it." "Son-in-law, you spoke the truth; father-in-law, you spoke a lie. Honor your son-in-law."
uncertain: h₁íd widóm: speaker of 'I saw it' unclear (a witness? the son-in-law himself?)
h₁sónt: ACC.SG neuter 'the true thing, truth'

english: A man made an oath and broke it. The gods saw him. Then his barley perished, his house sank down, and his offspring is gone. Then death seized him, and no one honored him. The fire guards the oath. The man died; the oath did not die.

Father Sky, you who protect the guest, guard him [on the] paths. Mother Earth, carry him. May his path be straight, may a star show him the way, and may the sun warm him. May the wolf not seize him. May he come to his own home, and may his mother see him.
uncertain: h₁ésmey stéygʰm̥ woydéyoyh₁t: 'show the path to him' (causative 'make see')
misfit: stéygʰes: NOM.PL 'paths' or PST.2SG 'you were walking'; neither fits 'guard him ___'; ACC.PL stéygʰn̥s or LOC.PL expected for 'on the paths'

english: It was growing dark, and a guest came to the king's dwelling. Then the king stood up, took his arm, led him inside and seated him on a seat. Then the queen brought him meat and honey. Then he ate and was sated. The king said: "Lie down. When dawn grows bright, tell me your name."
uncertain: sédesi: LOC.SG 'on a seat' (also verb SBJV/PRS.2SG)

english: Two sons stood up against [each other]. Then the mother stood between them and said: "You were born from me. I nourished you. Sons, you are striking me. Let no one kill his own brother." Then the two heard her and sat down on the ground. Peace came to the two of them.
uncertain: ǵeǵn̥h₁é, wos: PRF.2PL and plural pronoun for a pair of sons (dual expected)

stundtóm: PST.2DU 'you were striking me' or IMP.2DU 'strike me (instead)'; the imperative reading ('Sons, strike me; let no one kill his own brother') is coherent and perhaps better; English gives the indicative
tóh₁: NOM.DU 'those two' / ACC.DU 'to the two' or INS 'thereby'

english: Last year the master gave the guest a yoke. Yesterday the guest, carrying a gift, came back to the master's house. Then he looked at it and rejoiced, and he said: "A gift went out of my house, and a gift has come back to my house. Sit with me and eat." Then the two ate.
uncertain: déh₃rom / dóh₃r̥ / déh₃nom: three 'gift' words, not distinguished in English

english: King, I have made this pledge. I shall go forward. May I not flee. I shall die or win undying fame. Sky, you have seen me. If I flee, may the earth swallow me. My name shall become famous.
uncertain: pró: preverb 'forward' (analyzer also offers MID.AOR of pert-)
méroh₂ wénoh₂-wē: 'I shall die or I shall win'

english: This one broke that one's boat. Then the king said: "If anyone takes his brother's boat and the boat sinks, let him give him a boat. If the brother gives it [to him] and it sinks, let him give nothing. The boat is the brother's [risk]."
uncertain: h₁íh₂m̥ / h₁íh₂: feminine anaphor for néh₂us (f.)
néh₂us bʰréh₂tr̥s h₁ésti: 'the boat is the brother's'; sense of the closing maxim unclear (loss falls on the lender?)
mē kʷid déh₃ut: prohibitive 'let him give nothing'

english: The guest ate and drank. Then he [the host] spoke: "Guest, are you satisfied? Who are you? Where are you going? Is your mother alive?" "I am a shepherd's son. I am going to my brother's house. My mother is alive; my father is not alive." "Lie down on my seat, and may the night bring you rest." Then he lay down.
uncertain: speaker of mléwHt: unnamed, taken as host
misfit: méh₂ter: VOC.SG used as subject of gʷíh₃weti ('does your mother live?'); NOM méh₂tēr expected (as used two sentences later)

english: Father Sky, hear me. Mother Earth, listen. I did not steal my kinsman's horse. If I speak a lie, Sky, may you strike me down, and may the earth not nourish me. If I speak the truth, may I live and see the dawn, and may my house stand.
misfit: ph₂térm̥: ACC.SG in an invocation next to VOC dyéw ('Father Sky, hear me'); VOC ph₂ter expected

english: The guest stood up, and the master went with him and said: "This ford that is in my field, that is your path. Go in peace. Remember this house. If you come back to my house, I shall honor you."
uncertain: ḱód ... sth₂éh₁yeti: relative-like 'this (ford) that stands', no relative pronoun
ḱóm dṓm: 'this house' (ḱóm ACC.SG) vs preposition 'with'

english: A man went to the king and spoke: "My brother's cattle ate my barley. What will he give me?" Then he [the king] said: "Let him give you barley and build a fence. A fence keeps the peace." Then he built a fence.
Kinsmen, listen! The fight devoured men. Let the earth cover the slain, and let peace be a shelter for you. Let the fight lie down. Lift the plough and plough the field. May the two households live.
uncertain: ḱléwsete / tl̥nh₂té / h₂éryete: PRS/PST/IMP 2PL; imperative read

english: The priest said to the king: "Sacrifice to the god Werunos (Varuna)."
uncertain: ǵʰéwtōr: no gloss in lexicon; from ǵʰew- 'pour' = 'libation-pourer, priest'
wérunom: not analyzed; proper name Werunos (cf. Varuna), ACC
text uses a different spelling convention (wewked, tom)

english: Then the sheep said to the horses: "My heart is pained, seeing a man driving horses."
uncertain: widn̥tbʰ(y)os: not analyzed; DAT.PL participle 'for (those) seeing', plural vs singular moi ('us sheep'?)
Héǵontm̥: ACC.SG participle of h₂eǵ- 'driving', Hnérm̥ ACC 'man'

english: The sheep said to the horses: "My heart is pained, seeing a man driving horses."
uncertain: h₂gʰnutoy, widntéy, dʰǵʰmónm, h₂éǵontm: not analyzed (different spelling convention); read as 'is pained', DAT.SG participle 'to (me) seeing', ACC 'man (earthling)', ACC participle 'driving'

english: A gift seeks a gift. He who gives receives; he who does not give does not receive. A gift is not lost. The gift of a good heart is dear. The giver of good things is a friend.
uncertain: déh₃nom h₁uséws ḱr̥dés: 'gift of a good heart' (or 'dear to a good heart')

english: "Whose son are you?" "I am the son of your father's guest-friend." "He ate at my seat. This house gave him a horse, and he gave [us] a wagon. Now I know you, and you are my friend. Eat at my fire, and I shall give you a gift. Let the bond between the two houses not be broken."
uncertain: só moy sédesi h₁édt: speaker unclear; 'he ate at my seat'
ḱós dṓm: read as one NP 'this house' (dṓm NOM.SG, masc.) as subject of déh₃t; alternative 'this one ... home' less likely
